title: 36 cells, 4 rules. Every 30 generations it fires a glider. 50 of them by generation 1,500.
description:
Conway's Game of Life on an unbounded grid, starting from the 36 live cells of the Gosper glider gun (Bill Gosper, 1970). No seed, no randomness: the four rules run exactly. A live cell with two or three live neighbors survives, a dead cell with exactly three live neighbors is born, every other cell dies or stays dead. Gliders are counted as five-cell components that match one of the four glider phases and have separated from the gun.

Measured over 3,200 generations:
- the first glider separates from the gun at generation 15
- launches happen every 30 generations exactly: 107 gliders by generation 3,200, spacing between launches always 30
- the gun returns to the same 36 cells at every multiple of 30, and no shorter period works
- the gun never leaves a 36 by 9 cell box
- live cells 30 generations later minus live cells now: always exactly 5, at every generation from 0 to 3,170
- generation 1,500: 50 gliders launched, 286 cells alive
- generation 3,000: 100 gliders launched, 536 cells alive
- the leading glider moves one diagonal cell every 4.00 generations (0.2500 cells per generation in each axis)

The scene shows the first 3,138 generations; the playback rate ramps from 4 to 100 generations per second.

The numbers in the narration are the printed outputs of this exact run.

Made end to end by an AI agent: simulation, footage, voice, music, and edit.
